resources.string: Its capped sum of wakelock time was %1$s; overlapping wakelocks can count more than once.

plurals.name: nc_reason_app_wakeups
plurals.item: It woke the phone %1$d time in the night, so Android could not stay in deep sleep.
It woke the phone %1$d times in the night, so Android could not stay in deep sleep.

resources.string: Google Play warns about long wakelocks with the screen off; Android does not show screen state or exemptions for these counters.
Android never reached deep Doze, and the phone was in deep sleep only %1$s of the night.
The phone was in deep sleep only %1$s of the night.
The phone was in deep sleep only %1$s of the night, usually %2$s.
No app stands out: Android itself did not reach deep sleep. Often a system bug after an update, or a weak mobile signal.
No app stands out, and the mobile signal was weak: searching for the network keeps Android awake.
Something kept the phone awake: an app or Android itself.
%1$s with the screen off, with %2$s deep sleep.
%1$s with the screen off, usually %2$s, with %3$s deep sleep.
The phone slept, so no app kept it awake. The power went to the radio (mobile network, 5G) or the hardware.
The mobile signal was weak: the radio needs much more power to hold the network.
No night recorded. Activity+ records the night while its live status is on.
The phone was charging overnight. Android does not Doze while charging, so there is nothing to judge.
The screen was never off for 3 hours at a stretch last night.
Which apps were awake in the night? With a read permission on the pro page, Activity+ names them.
A bug in an update is usually fixed by the next one. Apps allowed to skip battery optimisation also skip Doze.
Wi-Fi at night, or Wi-Fi calling, lets the mobile radio rest. Activity+ never changes this itself.
Android\'s battery usage shows what drew the power.
Deep sleep is the time the processor was switched off. Doze is Android\'s way to get there: it holds back apps until the phone lies still.
